claims: "as well as the custom of communities in New York and New Jersey" - The transcript mentions these communities at the very end as the current practitioners, but the teacher does not examine the customs of these specific communities as a subject of the class.
summary: Mr. Arking discusses the laws and customs surrounding praying Arbit before sunset, examining the opinions in the Gmarrah and Shulhan Aruch, as well as the custom of communities in New York and New Jersey. He explores the views of authorities such as Maran, Rabenu Tam, the Rosh, Rabbi Yisraeli Ya'akov Algazi, the Arizal, and the Ben Ish Hai.
questions: Can someone pray Arbit before sunset?
What is the ruling in Shulhan Aruch regarding praying Minha after Pelig Minha and Arbit before sunset?
How does the custom in our communities compare to the ruling of Maran?
What was the practice of the Arizal regarding Arbit?
How do we handle Friday night Arbit compared to weeknights?
